traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements for Story 008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX are implemented and verified.
• Core functionality (ESLint --fix): Implemented via `meta.fixable = "code"` and fixer callbacks in `require-story-annotation` (for missing @story on functions/methods, TS declare functions, TS method signatures) and `valid-annotation-format` (for simple @story suffix normalization). `tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts` exercises these behaviors with before/after code comparisons and all tests pass under Jest.
• Safety and preservation: Fixers are conservative. `createAddStoryFix` and `createMethodFix` only insert a single JSDoc line at a computed insertion boundary, without changing existing code or comments. `getFixedStoryPath` only adjusts the `.story`/`.md` suffix and explicitly refuses paths with `..`. `createStoryFix` finds and replaces only the @story value substring; if it cannot safely locate it, it returns null and the rule falls back to reporting without a fix. This matches REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE and REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE.
• Integration with existing rules/toolchain: Auto-fix is built into the existing validation rules (`require-story-annotation`, `valid-annotation-format`) rather than separate utilities, and uses standard ESLint rule metadata and `context.report({ fix })` patterns. The passing Jest RuleTester suites confirm these rules behave correctly when run in fix mode.
• User experience and consistency: Tests cover a representative set of code patterns (function declarations, function expressions, class methods, TS declare functions, TS method signatures) and confirm both that already-correct code remains unchanged and that fixes are applied consistently when violations exist. Suffix normalization tests cover `.story`→`.story.md` and bare base path→`.story.md` scenarios.
• Error handling for non-fixable cases: For `valid-annotation-format`, if the @story tag or its value range cannot be safely derived, `createStoryFix` returns null and `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix` intentionally falls back to a non-fix reporting path. For story values with internal whitespace or paths that still do not match the required pattern after attempted normalization, the rule reports errors without applying fixes.
• Configurable templates (REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE): `require-story-annotation` exposes `annotationTemplate` and `methodAnnotationTemplate` options, which are fed through `require-story-helpers` into `coreReportMissing`/`coreReportMethod`. Tests explicitly verify that custom templates are used when supplied.
• Selective enable/disable (REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE): `require-story-annotation` supports an `autoFix` boolean option that controls whether the fixer is attached; tests confirm that when `autoFix: false` is configured, the rule still reports an error but does not change output. `valid-annotation-format` similarly includes an `autoFix` rule option; `validateStoryAnnotation` checks `options.autoFix !== false` before attaching a fix, otherwise it only reports the invalid format.
• Documentation: `user-docs/api-reference.md` documents the `--fix` behavior, the configurable templates, and the `autoFix` toggles for both rules, aligning with the behavior in code.
Given the passing targeted tests, presence of configuration and fix logic matching all REQ-AUTOFIX-* items, safe handling of edge cases, and up-to-date user documentation, this story is fully implemented.
